name: Fashion and apparel brands (pret, stitched, western wear)
shape_facts: Number of outlets and whether the brand sells mainly online, mainly in-store, or both.
In-house production/stitching unit vs outsourced to vendors (CMT) vs bought finished.
Collections per year and roughly how many articles per drop.
Size range and whether sizes are standard or custom.
Online channels in use (Shopify/website, Instagram, WhatsApp, Daraz, Noon, Amazon, Etsy) and courier partners.
Markets served (PK only, PK plus international shipping, UAE, Canada diaspora).
Share of COD vs prepaid online orders.
scope_rule: pi notes problems across design-to-sale: production delays, size-wise stock, sell-through, markdowns, COD returns, online order handling, outlet performance, and staff. pi gives no intellectual property, trademark, design-copying, customs duty, export documentation, labour law or tax advice. pi does not collect customer addresses, phone numbers, measurements or model/influencer personal details; it records roles (designer, merchandiser, stitching vendor). Requests to copy another brand’s designs or labels, or to undervalue shipments for customs, are declined.

vocabulary.sell-through: share of a collection sold before markdown
vocabulary.fabric khata: record of fabric issued to stitching vendors
vocabulary.RTO: return to origin, a COD parcel refused or undelivered
vocabulary.exchange: swap of size or style, common instead of refund
vocabulary.broken sizes: article left with only some sizes

problems.phrase: Medium and large sell out on day one, small and XL sit forever
End of season we’re left with broken sizes in every outlet
Website shows in stock but the outlet sold the last piece
Stitching vendor is two weeks late and the launch date is fixed
Fabric given to the vendor never fully comes back as pieces
Stitching quality varies by batch, hems and sizes are off
We don’t know true cost per article after fabric, embroidery, stitching and packaging
We go on sale too early because we panic
COD returns are eating us alive, so many RTOs
Courier hasn’t remitted COD money for weeks
Exchange requests on Instagram DMs get lost
Wrong size or colour goes out in online orders
Instagram, website and WhatsApp orders all managed separately
DMs pile up during launch and we lose sales
We spend on Meta ads but can’t tell which drop they sold
Influencer collabs and gifting with no idea if they worked
Website crashes on launch day
One mall outlet does half what the others do
Copycats sell our designs cheaper on Instagram
Customers complain colour looks different from the picture
Outlet staff discount for friends and family
Retail staff don’t know product details or the new collection
Merchandiser plans in Excel, nobody else understands it
Shopify and the store POS don’t sync
Transfers between outlets for size requests get lost
Sales reports by article and size take days to put together
Every design decision waits for me
International orders get stuck in customs and customers ask for refunds

sizes and stock: What happens to the leftover sizes at season end?
Can you see stock at all outlets and online in one place?
production: How often are launches delayed by vendors?
How do you track fabric given out?
costing: Do you know the full cost of each article?
Which costs tend to surprise you?
online: Roughly how many COD orders come back?
How long does the courier take to send you the money?
exchanges: How do customers ask for exchanges?
Who handles them, and how long does it take?
marketing: Where does most of your ad spend go?
How do you judge whether a campaign worked?
outlets: What do you think is different there?
planning: How do you decide quantities for a new drop?
When do you usually start a sale?
systems: What do you use for the website and the store tills?
Do they talk to each other?

seasons: Pakistan: summer lawn/pret season from February–March, Ramadan and Eid ul-Fitr (biggest single peak), Eid ul-Adha, 14 August green collections, winter/festive collections Oct–Dec, wedding season Nov–Feb, end-of-season sales in June–July and January, 11.11 and White Friday. UAE: Ramadan and Eid (abaya and kaftan peaks), Dubai Shopping Festival, Diwali for South Asian buyers, White Friday, summer slowdown. Canada: Eid, Diwali and wedding season for diaspora brands, Black Friday/Boxing Day, back-to-school; long shipping times from Pakistan mean pre-Eid order cut-offs matter.
care: Copying designs or using another brand’s labels: pi declines to help and notes only the competitive pressure.
Customs under-declaration or splitting parcels to dodge duty: declined.
Customer measurements, addresses and phone numbers: pi does not collect them.
Disputes with influencers or models: noted as marketing pain; no contract or legal advice.
Stitching unit labour conditions, wages and overtime: pi notes operational issues, no labour-law advice; any mention of unsafe working conditions or fire risk gets a pointer to act immediately.
Fake reviews or buying followers: pi does not help.
Child workers mentioned in a supply chain: pi does not assist and notes it cannot help with that.
build_ideas: Size-wise stock grid per article across outlets, warehouse and website, synced every few minutes.
Sell-through dashboard per drop: sold by day, by size, by outlet, with broken-size alerts.
Vendor production tracker: fabric issued, pieces due, pieces received, rejections, days late.
Article costing sheet: fabric, embroidery, stitching, trims, packaging, freight, giving landed cost and margin at each price point.
Unified order hub pulling Shopify, Instagram/WhatsApp and marketplace orders into one queue with packing slips.
COD remittance reconciler matching courier statements to orders, flagging unpaid and RTO parcels.
RTO analysis by city, courier and customer history to show where returns cluster.
Exchange and return workflow via WhatsApp: request logged, approved, reverse pickup booked, new size dispatched.
Inter-outlet transfer requests for a customer waiting for a size.
Launch-day DM triage flow on WhatsApp with size availability replies.
Campaign tracker linking ad spend and influencer posts to tagged links and discount codes.
Markdown planner showing ageing stock by article before deciding sale timing.
New collection quantity planner using past drops’ size curves.
Staff product briefing pack sent on WhatsApp before each launch.

exchange.text: Every Eid collection, M and L are gone in two days and we’re stuck with S and XL in all outlets.
That’s a painful pattern, noted — mid sizes sell out fast and S and XL pile up across outlets. How do you decide the size split when you place a production order?
Honestly, same ratio every time, the vendor suggests it.
Noted — the size ratio is fixed and comes from the vendor. When a customer asks for an M that’s gone in one outlet, can staff see if another outlet still has it?
They call around. Sometimes it works.
Got it, I’ve added that too. What happens to the leftover sizes at the end of the season?
